Give an exact answer.

$$
\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{6}} \frac{7}{\sqrt{1 - 9 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$"] [:db/add "8d27d9cf-cb74-5840-b365-e7db0c04fb39" :question/worked-solution "Use the linear substitution $u=3 x.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=3,\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\frac{1}{3})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Change both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=0&\Longrightarrow u=(3)(0)=0 \\ x=\frac{1}{6}&\Longrightarrow u=(3)(\frac{1}{6})=\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Both transformed endpoints lie strictly between $-1$ and $1$, so the integrand is continuous throughout the interval.

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int_{0}^{\frac{1}{6}} \frac{7}{\sqrt{1 - 9 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 7\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{6}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(3 x)^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 7(\frac{1}{3})\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{7}{3}\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{7}{3}[\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}]_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}} \\  &= \frac{7}{3}(\operatorname{arcsin}(\frac{1}{2})-\operatorname{arcsin}(0)) \\  &= \frac{7}{3}((\frac{\pi}{6})-(0)) \\  &= \frac{7 \pi}{18}\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "8d27d9cf-cb74-5840-b365-e7db0c04fb39" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] [:db/add "8d27d9cf-cb74-5840-b365-e7db0c04fb39" :question/answer-fields $$
\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{6}} \frac{8}{36 x^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$"] [:db/add "a497f451-04d7-5c60-a172-42abdf02370f" :question/worked-solution "Use the linear substitution $u=6 x.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=6,\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\frac{1}{6})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Change both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=0&\Longrightarrow u=(6)(0)=0 \\ x=\frac{1}{6}&\Longrightarrow u=(6)(\frac{1}{6})=1\end{aligned}
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int_{0}^{\frac{1}{6}} \frac{8}{36 x^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 8\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{6}} \frac{1}{1+(6 x)^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 8(\frac{1}{6})\int_{0}^{1} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{4}{3}\int_{0}^{1} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{4}{3}[\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}]_{0}^{1} \\  &= \frac{4}{3}(\operatorname{arctan}(1)-\operatorname{arctan}(0)) \\  &= \frac{4}{3}((\frac{\pi}{4})-(0)) \\  &= \frac{\pi}{3}\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "a497f451-04d7-5c60-a172-42abdf02370f" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] [:db/add "a497f451-04d7-5c60-a172-42abdf02370f" :question/answer-fields Give an exact answer.

$$
\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{14}} \frac{6}{49 x^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$"] [:db/add "24b61c76-ca28-5b5c-9a6e-51d22a7f675a" :question/worked-solution "Use the linear substitution $u=7 x.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=7,\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\frac{1}{7})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Change both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=0&\Longrightarrow u=(7)(0)=0 \\ x=\frac{1}{14}&\Longrightarrow u=(7)(\frac{1}{14})=\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int_{0}^{\frac{1}{14}} \frac{6}{49 x^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 6\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{14}} \frac{1}{1+(7 x)^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 6(\frac{1}{7})\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{6}{7}\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{6}{7}[\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}]_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}} \\  &= \frac{6}{7}(\operatorname{arctan}(\frac{1}{2})-\operatorname{arctan}(0)) \\  &= \frac{6}{7}((\operatorname{arctan}{\left(\frac{1}{2} \right)})-(0)) \\  &= \frac{6 \operatorname{arctan}{\left(\frac{1}{2} \right)}}{7}\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "24b61c76-ca28-5b5c-9a6e-51d22a7f675a" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] [:db/add "24b61c76-ca28-5b5c-9a6e-51d22a7f675a" :question/answer-fields "39a7f2e1-904a-5576-a7b2-3a71b7ec4a32"] [:db/ensure "24b61c76-ca28-5b5c-9a6e-51d22a7f675a" :question/validate] [:db/add 17592186064220 :knowledge-point/questions "24b61c76-ca28-5b5c-9a6e-51d22a7f675a"] [:db/add "3e664b4d-38a8-5ddc-9c88-53307ae3c5bd" :answer/id #uuid "3e664b4d-38a8-5ddc-9c88-53307ae3c5bd"] [:db/add "3e664b4d-38a8-5ddc-9c88-53307ae3c5bd" :answer/type :answer.type/math] [:db/add "3e664b4d-38a8-5ddc-9c88-53307ae3c5bd" :answer/value "\frac{2 \pi}{15}"] [:db/ensure "3e664b4d-38a8-5ddc-9c88-53307ae3c5bd" :answer/validate] [:db/add "aa4440e7-6f62-5402-bbe0-f2650309cdb7" :answer-field/id #uuid "aa4440e7-6f62-5402-bbe0-f2650309cdb7"] [:db/add "aa4440e7-6f62-5402-bbe0-f2650309cdb7" :answer-field/key "answer"] [:db/add "aa4440e7-6f62-5402-bbe0-f2650309cdb7" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/blank] [:db/add "aa4440e7-6f62-5402-bbe0-f2650309cdb7" :answer-field/choices "3e664b4d-38a8-5ddc-9c88-53307ae3c5bd"] [:db/add "aa4440e7-6f62-5402-bbe0-f2650309cdb7" :answer-field/correct "3e664b4d-38a8-5ddc-9c88-53307ae3c5bd"] [:db/ensure "aa4440e7-6f62-5402-bbe0-f2650309cdb7" :answer-field/validate] [:db/add "a2d73b9e-ded5-5263-8f8f-f603b91d7e83" :question/id #uuid "a2d73b9e-ded5-5263-8f8f-f603b91d7e83"] [:db/add "a2d73b9e-ded5-5263-8f8f-f603b91d7e83" :question/problem "Evaluate the integral. $$

$$

$$

Change both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=0&\Longrightarrow u=(9)(0)=0 \\ x=\frac{1}{9}&\Longrightarrow u=(9)(\frac{1}{9})=1\end{aligned}
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int_{0}^{\frac{1}{9}} \frac{9}{81 x^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 9\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{9}} \frac{1}{1+(9 x)^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 9(\frac{1}{9})\int_{0}^{1} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= 1\int_{0}^{1} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= 1[\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}]_{0}^{1} \\  &= 1(\operatorname{arctan}(1)-\operatorname{arctan}(0)) \\  &= 1((\frac{\pi}{4})-(0)) \\  &= \frac{\pi}{4}\end{aligned}

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=8,\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\frac{1}{8})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Change both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=0&\Longrightarrow u=(8)(0)=0 \\ x=\frac{1}{8}&\Longrightarrow u=(8)(\frac{1}{8})=1\end{aligned}
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

Give an exact answer.

$$
\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}} \frac{8}{36 x^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$"] [:db/add "7f635271-ad06-57ec-ba14-197476f846bc" :question/worked-solution "Use the linear substitution $u=6 x.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=6,\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\frac{1}{6})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Change both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=0&\Longrightarrow u=(6)(0)=0 \\ x=\frac{1}{2}&\Longrightarrow u=(6)(\frac{1}{2})=3\end{aligned}
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}} \frac{8}{36 x^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 8\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}} \frac{1}{1+(6 x)^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 8(\frac{1}{6})\int_{0}^{3} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{4}{3}\int_{0}^{3} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{4}{3}[\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}]_{0}^{3} \\  &= \frac{4}{3}(\operatorname{arctan}(3)-\operatorname{arctan}(0)) \\  &= \frac{4}{3}((\operatorname{arctan}{\left(3 \right)})-(0)) \\  &= \frac{4 \operatorname{arctan}{\left(3 \right)}}{3}\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "7f635271-ad06-57ec-ba14-197476f846bc" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] [:db/add "7f635271-ad06-57ec-ba14-197476f846bc" :question/answer-fields "708a5c04-84ae-5fc7-8d2f-1654bd8d1621"] [:db/ensure "7f635271-ad06-57ec-ba14-197476f846bc" :question/validate] [:db/add 17592186064220 :knowledge-point/questions "7f635271-ad06-57ec-ba14-197476f846bc"] [:db/add "1af8cc77-0bac-5940-b352-f949e5f99a1a" :answer/id #uuid "1af8cc77-0bac-5940-b352-f949e5f99a1a"] [:db/add "1af8cc77-0bac-5940-b352-f949e5f99a1a" :answer/type :answer.type/math] [:db/add "1af8cc77-0bac-5940-b352-f949e5f99a1a" :answer/value "\frac{\pi}{15}"] [:db/ensure "1af8cc77-0bac-5940-b352-f949e5f99a1a" :answer/validate] [:db/add "0ee451c8-40b1-5552-b4a2-16770a8b9dcd" :answer-field/id #uuid "0ee451c8-40b1-5552-b4a2-16770a8b9dcd"] [:db/add "0ee451c8-40b1-5552-b4a2-16770a8b9dcd" :answer-field/key "answer"] [:db/add "0ee451c8-40b1-5552-b4a2-16770a8b9dcd" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/blank] [:db/add "0ee451c8-40b1-5552-b4a2-16770a8b9dcd" :answer-field/choices "1af8cc77-0bac-5940-b352-f949e5f99a1a"] [:db/add "0ee451c8-40b1-5552-b4a2-16770a8b9dcd" :answer-field/correct "1af8cc77-0bac-5940-b352-f949e5f99a1a"] [:db/ensure "0ee451c8-40b1-5552-b4a2-16770a8b9dcd" :answer-field/validate] [:db/add "b8833921-cd55-5d33-86f3-5cb87a7b71f5" :question/id #uuid "b8833921-cd55-5d33-86f3-5cb87a7b71f5"] [:db/add "b8833921-cd55-5d33-86f3-5cb87a7b71f5" :question/problem "Evaluate the integral. $$

{{answer}}"] [:db/add "b8833921-cd55-5d33-86f3-5cb87a7b71f5" :question/worked-solution "Use the linear substitution $u=5 x.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=5,\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\frac{1}{5})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Change both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=0&\Longrightarrow u=(5)(0)=0 \\ x=\frac{1}{10}&\Longrightarrow u=(5)(\frac{1}{10})=\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Both transformed endpoints lie strictly between $-1$ and $1$, so the integrand is continuous throughout the interval.

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int_{0}^{\frac{1}{10}} \frac{2}{\sqrt{1 - 25 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 2\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{10}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(5 x)^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 2(\frac{1}{5})\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{2}{5}\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{2}{5}[\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}]_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}} \\  &= \frac{2}{5}(\operatorname{arcsin}(\frac{1}{2})-\operatorname{arcsin}(0)) \\  &= \frac{2}{5}((\frac{\pi}{6})-(0)) \\  &= \frac{\pi}{15}\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "b8833921-cd55-5d33-86f3-5cb87a7b71f5" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] [:db/add "b8833921-cd55-5d33-86f3-5cb87a7b71f5" :question/answer-fields "e251937d-16b7-5326-a140-cdc3ea29c25f" :question/id #uuid "e251937d-16b7-5326-a140-cdc3ea29c25f"] [:db/add "e251937d-16b7-5326-a140-cdc3ea29c25f" :question/problem "Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int_{0}^{3 \sqrt{2}} \frac{2}{x^{2} + 6}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$"] [:db/add "e251937d-16b7-5326-a140-cdc3ea29c25f" :question/worked-solution "First factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
x^{2} + 6=6(1+(\frac{1}{6})x^{2})
$$

Use the linear substitution $u=\frac{\sqrt{6} x}{6}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{\sqrt{6}}{6},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\sqrt{6})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Change both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=0&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{\sqrt{6}}{6})(0)=0 \\ x=3 \sqrt{2}&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{\sqrt{6}}{6})(3 \sqrt{2})=\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int_{0}^{3 \sqrt{2}} \frac{2}{x^{2} + 6}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{1}{3}\int_{0}^{3 \sqrt{2}} \frac{1}{1+(\frac{\sqrt{6} x}{6})^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{1}{3}(\sqrt{6})\int_{0}^{\sqrt{3}} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}\int_{0}^{\sqrt{3}} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}[\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}]_{0}^{\sqrt{3}} \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}(\operatorname{arctan}(\sqrt{3})-\operatorname{arctan}(0)) \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}((\frac{\pi}{3})-(0)) \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{6} \pi}{9}\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "e251937d-16b7-5326-a140-cdc3ea29c25f" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "e251937d-16b7-5326-a140-cdc3ea29c25f" :question/answer-fields Give an exact answer.

$$
\int_{0}^{\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}} \frac{2}{\sqrt{2 - x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$"] [:db/add "3678de14-c7a3-5309-a87e-827f356a473e" :question/worked-solution "First factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
\sqrt{2 - x^{2}}=\sqrt{2(1-(\frac{1}{2})x^{2})}
$$

Use the linear substitution $u=\frac{\sqrt{2} x}{2}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\sqrt{2})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Change both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=0&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})(0)=0 \\ x=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})=\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Both transformed endpoints lie strictly between $-1$ and $1$, so the integrand is continuous throughout the interval.

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int_{0}^{\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}} \frac{2}{\sqrt{2 - x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \sqrt{2}\int_{0}^{\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(\frac{\sqrt{2} x}{2})^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \sqrt{2}(\sqrt{2})\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= 2\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= 2[\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}]_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}} \\  &= 2(\operatorname{arcsin}(\frac{1}{2})-\operatorname{arcsin}(0)) \\  &= 2((\frac{\pi}{6})-(0)) \\  &= \frac{\pi}{3}\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "3678de14-c7a3-5309-a87e-827f356a473e" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "3678de14-c7a3-5309-a87e-827f356a473e" :question/answer-fields Give an exact answer.

$$
\int_{0}^{6} \frac{3}{x^{2} + 36}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$"] [:db/add "e13e5fe8-8cb3-5e53-84d4-dc9d70dae4ca" :question/worked-solution "First factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
x^{2} + 36=36(1+(\frac{1}{36})x^{2})
$$

Use the linear substitution $u=\frac{x}{6}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{1}{6},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(6)\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Change both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=0&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{1}{6})(0)=0 \\ x=6&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{1}{6})(6)=1\end{aligned}
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int_{0}^{6} \frac{3}{x^{2} + 36}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{1}{12}\int_{0}^{6} \frac{1}{1+(\frac{x}{6})^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{1}{12}(6)\int_{0}^{1} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{1}{2}\int_{0}^{1} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{1}{2}[\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}]_{0}^{1} \\  &= \frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{arctan}(1)-\operatorname{arctan}(0)) \\  &= \frac{1}{2}((\frac{\pi}{4})-(0)) \\  &= \frac{\pi}{8}\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "e13e5fe8-8cb3-5e53-84d4-dc9d70dae4ca" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "e13e5fe8-8cb3-5e53-84d4-dc9d70dae4ca" :question/answer-fields $$
\int_{0}^{\frac{5 \sqrt{2}}{2}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{25 - x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x

$$
\sqrt{25 - x^{2}}=\sqrt{25(1-(\frac{1}{25})x^{2})}
$$

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{1}{5},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(5)\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Change both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=0&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{1}{5})(0)=0 \\ x=\frac{5 \sqrt{2}}{2}&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{1}{5})(\frac{5 \sqrt{2}}{2})=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Both transformed endpoints lie strictly between $-1$ and $1$, so the integrand is continuous throughout the interval.

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int_{0}^{\frac{5 \sqrt{2}}{2}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{25 - x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{1}{5}\int_{0}^{\frac{5 \sqrt{2}}{2}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(\frac{x}{5})^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{1}{5}(5)\int_{0}^{\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= 1\int_{0}^{\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= 1[\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}]_{0}^{\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}} \\  &= 1(\operatorname{arcsin}(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})-\operatorname{arcsin}(0)) \\  &= 1((\frac{\pi}{4})-(0)) \\  &= \frac{\pi}{4}\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "682222db-91f6-5331-b0ae-5361f8ce335b" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "682222db-91f6-5331-b0ae-5361f8ce335b" :question/answer-fields Give an exact answer.

$$
\int_{-3}^{3} \frac{2}{\sqrt{36 - x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$"] [:db/add "e4cdc649-5543-52c4-9e7e-a603083141ff" :question/worked-solution "First factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
\sqrt{36 - x^{2}}=\sqrt{36(1-(\frac{1}{36})x^{2})}
$$

Use the linear substitution $u=\frac{x}{6}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{1}{6},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(6)\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Change both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=-3&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{1}{6})(-3)=- \frac{1}{2} \\ x=3&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{1}{6})(3)=\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Both transformed endpoints lie strictly between $-1$ and $1$, so the integrand is continuous throughout the interval.

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int_{-3}^{3} \frac{2}{\sqrt{36 - x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{1}{3}\int_{-3}^{3} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(\frac{x}{6})^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{1}{3}(6)\int_{- \frac{1}{2}}^{\frac{1}{2}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= 2\int_{- \frac{1}{2}}^{\frac{1}{2}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= 2[\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}]_{- \frac{1}{2}}^{\frac{1}{2}} \\  &= 2(\operatorname{arcsin}(\frac{1}{2})-\operatorname{arcsin}(- \frac{1}{2})) \\  &= 2((\frac{\pi}{6})-(- \frac{\pi}{6})) \\  &= \frac{2 \pi}{3}\end{aligned}

{{answer}}"] [:db/add "21a4ebc8-c316-5cfd-93e4-ca1118604531" :question/worked-solution "First factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
x^{2} + 10=10(1+(\frac{1}{10})x^{2})
$$

Use the linear substitution $u=\frac{\sqrt{10} x}{10}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{\sqrt{10}}{10},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\sqrt{10})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Change both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=0&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{\sqrt{10}}{10})(0)=0 \\ x=\sqrt{10}&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{\sqrt{10}}{10})(\sqrt{10})=1\end{aligned}
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int_{0}^{\sqrt{10}} \frac{8}{x^{2} + 10}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{4}{5}\int_{0}^{\sqrt{10}} \frac{1}{1+(\frac{\sqrt{10} x}{10})^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{4}{5}(\sqrt{10})\int_{0}^{1} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{4 \sqrt{10}}{5}\int_{0}^{1} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{4 \sqrt{10}}{5}[\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}]_{0}^{1} \\  &= \frac{4 \sqrt{10}}{5}(\operatorname{arctan}(1)-\operatorname{arctan}(0)) \\  &= \frac{4 \sqrt{10}}{5}((\frac{\pi}{4})-(0)) \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{10} \pi}{5}\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "21a4ebc8-c316-5cfd-93e4-ca1118604531" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "21a4ebc8-c316-5cfd-93e4-ca1118604531" :question/answer-fields "5a9796b7-f543-5dc8-b952-8b55e73eb6a2"] [:db/ensure "21a4ebc8-c316-5cfd-93e4-ca1118604531" :question/validate] [:db/add 17592186064220 :knowledge-point/questions "21a4ebc8-c316-5cfd-93e4-ca1118604531"] [:db/add "cf36209d-dd8d-57a1-a765-f750e1391b98" :answer/id #uuid "cf36209d-dd8d-57a1-a765-f750e1391b98"] [:db/add "cf36209d-dd8d-57a1-a765-f750e1391b98" :answer/type :answer.type/math] [:db/add "cf36209d-dd8d-57a1-a765-f750e1391b98" :answer/value "\pi"] [:db/ensure "cf36209d-dd8d-57a1-a765-f750e1391b98" :answer/validate] [:db/add "b352b4d8-ef8e-542f-94af-6fac013fa473" :answer-field/id #uuid "b352b4d8-ef8e-542f-94af-6fac013fa473"] [:db/add "b352b4d8-ef8e-542f-94af-6fac013fa473" :answer-field/key "answer"] [:db/add "b352b4d8-ef8e-542f-94af-6fac013fa473" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/blank] [:db/add "b352b4d8-ef8e-542f-94af-6fac013fa473" :answer-field/choices "cf36209d-dd8d-57a1-a765-f750e1391b98"] [:db/add "b352b4d8-ef8e-542f-94af-6fac013fa473" :answer-field/correct "cf36209d-dd8d-57a1-a765-f750e1391b98"] [:db/ensure "b352b4d8-ef8e-542f-94af-6fac013fa473" :answer-field/validate] [:db/add "561f8902-181d-50e5-8116-48d2cb1ddaae" :question/id #uuid "561f8902-181d-50e5-8116-48d2cb1ddaae"] [:db/add "561f8902-181d-50e5-8116-48d2cb1ddaae" :question/problem "Evaluate the integral. "31069773-e2d9-58b9-845a-c488f05a3fd1" :question/id #uuid "31069773-e2d9-58b9-845a-c488f05a3fd1"] [:db/add "31069773-e2d9-58b9-845a-c488f05a3fd1" :question/problem "Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int_{- \frac{2 \sqrt{10}}{5}}^{\frac{2 \sqrt{30}}{5}} \frac{6}{\sqrt{64 - 10 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$"] [:db/add "31069773-e2d9-58b9-845a-c488f05a3fd1" :question/worked-solution "First factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
\sqrt{64 - 10 x^{2}}=\sqrt{64(1-(\frac{5}{32})x^{2})}
$$

Use the linear substitution $u=\frac{\sqrt{10} x}{8}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{\sqrt{10}}{8},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\frac{4 \sqrt{10}}{5})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Change both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=- \frac{2 \sqrt{10}}{5}&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{\sqrt{10}}{8})(- \frac{2 \sqrt{10}}{5})=- \frac{1}{2} \\ x=\frac{2 \sqrt{30}}{5}&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{\sqrt{10}}{8})(\frac{2 \sqrt{30}}{5})=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Both transformed endpoints lie strictly between $-1$ and $1$, so the integrand is continuous throughout the interval.

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int_{- \frac{2 \sqrt{10}}{5}}^{\frac{2 \sqrt{30}}{5}} \frac{6}{\sqrt{64 - 10 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{3}{4}\int_{- \frac{2 \sqrt{10}}{5}}^{\frac{2 \sqrt{30}}{5}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(\frac{\sqrt{10} x}{8})^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{3}{4}(\frac{4 \sqrt{10}}{5})\int_{- \frac{1}{2}}^{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{3 \sqrt{10}}{5}\int_{- \frac{1}{2}}^{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{3 \sqrt{10}}{5}[\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}]_{- \frac{1}{2}}^{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}} \\  &= \frac{3 \sqrt{10}}{5}(\operatorname{arcsin}(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})-\operatorname{arcsin}(- \frac{1}{2})) \\  &= \frac{3 \sqrt{10}}{5}((\frac{\pi}{3})-(- \frac{\pi}{6})) \\  &= \frac{3 \sqrt{10} \pi}{10}\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "31069773-e2d9-58b9-845a-c488f05a3fd1" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "31069773-e2d9-58b9-845a-c488f05a3fd1" :question/answer-fields Give an exact answer.

$$
\int_{\frac{5 \sqrt{21}}{21}}^{\frac{5 \sqrt{7}}{7}} \frac{9}{7 x^{2} + 25}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$"] [:db/add "4eddb1ed-78dc-5c0e-a58a-4f6c59d0a7cf" :question/worked-solution "First factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
7 x^{2} + 25=25(1+(\frac{7}{25})x^{2})
$$

Use the linear substitution $u=\frac{\sqrt{7} x}{5}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{\sqrt{7}}{5},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\frac{5 \sqrt{7}}{7})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Change both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\frac{5 \sqrt{21}}{21}&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{\sqrt{7}}{5})(\frac{5 \sqrt{21}}{21})=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3} \\ x=\frac{5 \sqrt{7}}{7}&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{\sqrt{7}}{5})(\frac{5 \sqrt{7}}{7})=1\end{aligned}
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int_{\frac{5 \sqrt{21}}{21}}^{\frac{5 \sqrt{7}}{7}} \frac{9}{7 x^{2} + 25}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{9}{25}\int_{\frac{5 \sqrt{21}}{21}}^{\frac{5 \sqrt{7}}{7}} \frac{1}{1+(\frac{\sqrt{7} x}{5})^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{9}{25}(\frac{5 \sqrt{7}}{7})\int_{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}}^{1} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{9 \sqrt{7}}{35}\int_{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}}^{1} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{9 \sqrt{7}}{35}[\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}]_{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}}^{1} \\  &= \frac{9 \sqrt{7}}{35}(\operatorname{arctan}(1)-\operatorname{arctan}(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3})) \\  &= \frac{9 \sqrt{7}}{35}((\frac{\pi}{4})-(\frac{\pi}{6})) \\  &= \frac{3 \sqrt{7} \pi}{140}\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "4eddb1ed-78dc-5c0e-a58a-4f6c59d0a7cf" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "4eddb1ed-78dc-5c0e-a58a-4f6c59d0a7cf" :question/answer-fields "275ef93a-9e15-50cd-b072-9c822daf3676" :question/id #uuid "275ef93a-9e15-50cd-b072-9c822daf3676"] [:db/add "275ef93a-9e15-50cd-b072-9c822daf3676" :question/problem "Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int_{- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{3}}^{\frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}} \frac{2}{6 x^{2} + 4}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$"] [:db/add "275ef93a-9e15-50cd-b072-9c822daf3676" :question/worked-solution "First factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
6 x^{2} + 4=4(1+(\frac{3}{2})x^{2})
$$

Use the linear substitution $u=\frac{\sqrt{6} x}{2}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{\sqrt{6}}{2},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\frac{\sqrt{6}}{3})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Change both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{3}&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{\sqrt{6}}{2})(- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{3})=- \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3} \\ x=\frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{\sqrt{6}}{2})(\frac{\sqrt{6}}{3})=1\end{aligned}
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int_{- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{3}}^{\frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}} \frac{2}{6 x^{2} + 4}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{1}{2}\int_{- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{3}}^{\frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}} \frac{1}{1+(\frac{\sqrt{6} x}{2})^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{1}{2}(\frac{\sqrt{6}}{3})\int_{- \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}}^{1} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{6}}{6}\int_{- \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}}^{1} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{6}}{6}[\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}]_{- \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}}^{1} \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{6}}{6}(\operatorname{arctan}(1)-\operatorname{arctan}(- \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3})) \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{6}}{6}((\frac{\pi}{4})-(- \frac{\pi}{6})) \\  &= \frac{5 \sqrt{6} \pi}{72}\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "275ef93a-9e15-50cd-b072-9c822daf3676" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "275ef93a-9e15-50cd-b072-9c822daf3676" :question/answer-fields $$

$$
\sqrt{36 - 6 x^{2}}=\sqrt{36(1-(\frac{1}{6})x^{2})}
$$

Use the linear substitution $u=\frac{\sqrt{6} x}{6}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{\sqrt{6}}{6},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\sqrt{6})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Change both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\frac{\sqrt{6}}{2}&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{\sqrt{6}}{6})(\frac{\sqrt{6}}{2})=\frac{1}{2} \\ x=\sqrt{3}&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{\sqrt{6}}{6})(\sqrt{3})=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Both transformed endpoints lie strictly between $-1$ and $1$, so the integrand is continuous throughout the interval.

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int_{\frac{\sqrt{6}}{2}}^{\sqrt{3}} \frac{5}{\sqrt{36 - 6 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{5}{6}\int_{\frac{\sqrt{6}}{2}}^{\sqrt{3}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(\frac{\sqrt{6} x}{6})^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{5}{6}(\sqrt{6})\int_{\frac{1}{2}}^{\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{5 \sqrt{6}}{6}\int_{\frac{1}{2}}^{\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{5 \sqrt{6}}{6}[\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}]_{\frac{1}{2}}^{\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}} \\  &= \frac{5 \sqrt{6}}{6}(\operatorname{arcsin}(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})-\operatorname{arcsin}(\frac{1}{2})) \\  &= \frac{5 \sqrt{6}}{6}((\frac{\pi}{4})-(\frac{\pi}{6})) \\  &= \frac{5 \sqrt{6} \pi}{72}\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "a4a4dc8e-8a02-5ef0-a5ce-5526bba8d539" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "a4a4dc8e-8a02-5ef0-a5ce-5526bba8d539" :question/answer-fields "c2f94dbd-24b0-502c-8bef-8dd471a94ea1"] [:db/ensure "a4a4dc8e-8a02-5ef0-a5ce-5526bba8d539" :question/validate] [:db/add 17592186064220 :knowledge-point/questions "a4a4dc8e-8a02-5ef0-a5ce-5526bba8d539"] [:db/add "094fa516-728f-5be6-a4fe-f67ece9b8145" :answer/id #uuid "094fa516-728f-5be6-a4fe-f67ece9b8145"] [:db/add "094fa516-728f-5be6-a4fe-f67ece9b8145" :answer/type :answer.type/math] [:db/add "094fa516-728f-5be6-a4fe-f67ece9b8145" :answer/value "\frac{3 \sqrt{6} \pi}{4}"] [:db/ensure "094fa516-728f-5be6-a4fe-f67ece9b8145" :answer/validate] [:db/add "ee3d0bc0-f989-584a-ae0f-e17e36f20d73" :answer-field/id #uuid "ee3d0bc0-f989-584a-ae0f-e17e36f20d73"] [:db/add "ee3d0bc0-f989-584a-ae0f-e17e36f20d73" :answer-field/key "answer"] [:db/add "ee3d0bc0-f989-584a-ae0f-e17e36f20d73" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/blank] [:db/add "ee3d0bc0-f989-584a-ae0f-e17e36f20d73" :answer-field/choices "094fa516-728f-5be6-a4fe-f67ece9b8145"] [:db/add "ee3d0bc0-f989-584a-ae0f-e17e36f20d73" :answer-field/correct "094fa516-728f-5be6-a4fe-f67ece9b8145"] [:db/ensure "ee3d0bc0-f989-584a-ae0f-e17e36f20d73" :answer-field/validate] [:db/add "d97ef683-6715-5e81-a7d1-14b2ffc5e533" :question/id #uuid "d97ef683-6715-5e81-a7d1-14b2ffc5e533"] [:db/add "d97ef683-6715-5e81-a7d1-14b2ffc5e533" :question/problem "Evaluate the integral. {{answer}}"] [:db/add "d97ef683-6715-5e81-a7d1-14b2ffc5e533" :question/worked-solution "First factor the constant in the denominator:

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}x=- \frac{\sqrt{6}}{4}&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{\sqrt{6}}{3})(- \frac{\sqrt{6}}{4})=- \frac{1}{2} \\ x=\frac{3 \sqrt{2}}{4}&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{\sqrt{6}}{3})(\frac{3 \sqrt{2}}{4})=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Both transformed endpoints lie strictly between $-1$ and $1$, so the integrand is continuous throughout the interval.

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int_{- \frac{\sqrt{6}}{4}}^{\frac{3 \sqrt{2}}{4}} \frac{9}{\sqrt{9 - 6 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 3\int_{- \frac{\sqrt{6}}{4}}^{\frac{3 \sqrt{2}}{4}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(\frac{\sqrt{6} x}{3})^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 3(\frac{\sqrt{6}}{2})\int_{- \frac{1}{2}}^{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{3 \sqrt{6}}{2}\int_{- \frac{1}{2}}^{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{3 \sqrt{6}}{2}[\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}]_{- \frac{1}{2}}^{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}} \\  &= \frac{3 \sqrt{6}}{2}(\operatorname{arcsin}(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})-\operatorname{arcsin}(- \frac{1}{2})) \\  &= \frac{3 \sqrt{6}}{2}((\frac{\pi}{3})-(- \frac{\pi}{6})) \\  &= \frac{3 \sqrt{6} \pi}{4}\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "d97ef683-6715-5e81-a7d1-14b2ffc5e533" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "d97ef683-6715-5e81-a7d1-14b2ffc5e533" :question/answer-fields "ee3d0bc0-f989-584a-ae0f-e17e36f20d73"] [:db/ensure "d97ef683-6715-5e81-a7d1-14b2ffc5e533" :question/validate] [:db/add 17592186064220 :knowledge-point/questions "d97ef683-6715-5e81-a7d1-14b2ffc5e533"] [:db/add "0a19f002-f394-581c-8a71-944f99d29f1c" :answer/id #uuid "0a19f002-f394-581c-8a71-944f99d29f1c"] [:db/add "0a19f002-f394-581c-8a71-944f99d29f1c" :answer/type :answer.type/math] [:db/add "0a19f002-f394-581c-8a71-944f99d29f1c" :answer/value "\frac{\sqrt{10} \pi}{360}"] [:db/ensure "0a19f002-f394-581c-8a71-944f99d29f1c" :answer/validate] [:db/add "b9486294-79c8-509d-84d4-b54229d994a1" :answer-field/id #uuid "b9486294-79c8-509d-84d4-b54229d994a1"] [:db/add "b9486294-79c8-509d-84d4-b54229d994a1" :answer-field/key "answer"] [:db/add "b9486294-79c8-509d-84d4-b54229d994a1" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/blank] [:db/add "b9486294-79c8-509d-84d4-b54229d994a1" :answer-field/choices "0a19f002-f394-581c-8a71-944f99d29f1c"] [:db/add "b9486294-79c8-509d-84d4-b54229d994a1" :answer-field/correct "0a19f002-f394-581c-8a71-944f99d29f1c"] [:db/ensure "b9486294-79c8-509d-84d4-b54229d994a1" :answer-field/validate] [:db/add "0372c2fd-66f2-541c-882f-7c71be7cc96e" :question/id #uuid "0372c2fd-66f2-541c-882f-7c71be7cc96e"] [:db/add "0372c2fd-66f2-541c-882f-7c71be7cc96e" :question/problem "Evaluate the integral. {{answer}}"] [:db/add "0372c2fd-66f2-541c-882f-7c71be7cc96e" :question/worked-solution "First factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
10 x^{2} + 9=9(1+(\frac{10}{9})x^{2})
$$

Use the linear substitution $u=\frac{\sqrt{10} x}{3}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{\sqrt{10}}{3},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\frac{3 \sqrt{10}}{10})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Change both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\frac{3 \sqrt{10}}{10}&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{\sqrt{10}}{3})(\frac{3 \sqrt{10}}{10})=1 \\ x=\frac{3 \sqrt{30}}{10}&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{\sqrt{10}}{3})(\frac{3 \sqrt{30}}{10})=\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int_{\frac{3 \sqrt{10}}{10}}^{\frac{3 \sqrt{30}}{10}} \frac{1}{10 x^{2} + 9}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{1}{9}\int_{\frac{3 \sqrt{10}}{10}}^{\frac{3 \sqrt{30}}{10}} \frac{1}{1+(\frac{\sqrt{10} x}{3})^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{1}{9}(\frac{3 \sqrt{10}}{10})\int_{1}^{\sqrt{3}} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{10}}{30}\int_{1}^{\sqrt{3}} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{10}}{30}[\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}]_{1}^{\sqrt{3}} \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{10}}{30}(\operatorname{arctan}(\sqrt{3})-\operatorname{arctan}(1)) \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{10}}{30}((\frac{\pi}{3})-(\frac{\pi}{4})) \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{10} \pi}{360}\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "0372c2fd-66f2-541c-882f-7c71be7cc96e" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "0372c2fd-66f2-541c-882f-7c71be7cc96e" :question/answer-fields "b9486294-79c8-509d-84d4-b54229d994a1"] [:db/ensure "0372c2fd-66f2-541c-882f-7c71be7cc96e" :question/validate] [:db/add 17592186064220 :knowledge-point/questions "0372c2fd-66f2-541c-882f-7c71be7cc96e"] [:db/add "fdc0d3f5-a51b-5597-9b0f-2b50228b93a1" :answer/id #uuid "fdc0d3f5-a51b-5597-9b0f-2b50228b93a1"] [:db/add "fdc0d3f5-a51b-5597-9b0f-2b50228b93a1" :answer/type :answer.type/math] [:db/add "fdc0d3f5-a51b-5597-9b0f-2b50228b93a1" :answer/value "\frac{7 \sqrt{3} \pi}{54}"] [:db/ensure "fdc0d3f5-a51b-5597-9b0f-2b50228b93a1" :answer/validate] [:db/add "d1b888f5-5707-53a5-b970-7313bcf41529" :answer-field/id #uuid "d1b888f5-5707-53a5-b970-7313bcf41529"] [:db/add "d1b888f5-5707-53a5-b970-7313bcf41529" :answer-field/key "answer"] [:db/add "d1b888f5-5707-53a5-b970-7313bcf41529" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/blank] [:db/add "d1b888f5-5707-53a5-b970-7313bcf41529" :answer-field/choices "fdc0d3f5-a51b-5597-9b0f-2b50228b93a1"] [:db/add "d1b888f5-5707-53a5-b970-7313bcf41529" :answer-field/correct "fdc0d3f5-a51b-5597-9b0f-2b50228b93a1"] [:db/ensure "d1b888f5-5707-53a5-b970-7313bcf41529" :answer-field/validate] [:db/add "5880c807-c10d-50e8-9d88-c434c7630fa9" :question/id #uuid "5880c807-c10d-50e8-9d88-c434c7630fa9"] [:db/add "5880c807-c10d-50e8-9d88-c434c7630fa9" :question/problem "Evaluate the integral. {{answer}}"] [:db/add "5880c807-c10d-50e8-9d88-c434c7630fa9" :question/worked-solution "First factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
3 x^{2} + 81=81(1+(\frac{1}{27})x^{2})
$$

Use the linear substitution $u=\frac{\sqrt{3} x}{9}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{9},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(3 \sqrt{3})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Change both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=- 3 \sqrt{3}&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{9})(- 3 \sqrt{3})=-1 \\ x=9&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{9})(9)=\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int_{- 3 \sqrt{3}}^{9} \frac{6}{3 x^{2} + 81}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{2}{27}\int_{- 3 \sqrt{3}}^{9} \frac{1}{1+(\frac{\sqrt{3} x}{9})^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{2}{27}(3 \sqrt{3})\int_{-1}^{\sqrt{3}} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{2 \sqrt{3}}{9}\int_{-1}^{\sqrt{3}} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{2 \sqrt{3}}{9}[\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}]_{-1}^{\sqrt{3}} \\  &= \frac{2 \sqrt{3}}{9}(\operatorname{arctan}(\sqrt{3})-\operatorname{arctan}(-1)) \\  &= \frac{2 \sqrt{3}}{9}((\frac{\pi}{3})-(- \frac{\pi}{4})) \\  &= \frac{7 \sqrt{3} \pi}{54}\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "5880c807-c10d-50e8-9d88-c434c7630fa9" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "5880c807-c10d-50e8-9d88-c434c7630fa9" :question/answer-fields "d1b888f5-5707-53a5-b970-7313bcf41529"] [:db/ensure "5880c807-c10d-50e8-9d88-c434c7630fa9" :question/validate] [:db/add 17592186064220 :knowledge-point/questions "5880c807-c10d-50e8-9d88-c434c7630fa9"] [:db/add "dad5e5d4-f28a-5e3c-9d7d-2ef281b00081" :answer/id #uuid "dad5e5d4-f28a-5e3c-9d7d-2ef281b00081"] [:db/add "dad5e5d4-f28a-5e3c-9d7d-2ef281b00081" :answer/type :answer.type/math] [:db/add "dad5e5d4-f28a-5e3c-9d7d-2ef281b00081" :answer/value "\frac{\sqrt{6} \pi}{36}"] [:db/ensure "dad5e5d4-f28a-5e3c-9d7d-2ef281b00081" :answer/validate] [:db/add "0970acb4-17e3-5133-8c74-81024d88697a" :answer-field/id #uuid "0970acb4-17e3-5133-8c74-81024d88697a"] [:db/add "0970acb4-17e3-5133-8c74-81024d88697a" :answer-field/key "answer"] [:db/add "0970acb4-17e3-5133-8c74-81024d88697a" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/blank] [:db/add "0970acb4-17e3-5133-8c74-81024d88697a" :answer-field/choices "dad5e5d4-f28a-5e3c-9d7d-2ef281b00081"] [:db/add "0970acb4-17e3-5133-8c74-81024d88697a" :answer-field/correct "dad5e5d4-f28a-5e3c-9d7d-2ef281b00081"] [:db/ensure "0970acb4-17e3-5133-8c74-81024d88697a" :answer-field/validate] [:db/add "26a5ab0e-8ab0-5f06-8396-7feffadcde08" :question/id #uuid "26a5ab0e-8ab0-5f06-8396-7feffadcde08"] [:db/add "26a5ab0e-8ab0-5f06-8396-7feffadcde08" :question/problem "Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int_{- \frac{9 \sqrt{10}}{20}}^{\frac{9 \sqrt{5}}{10}} \frac{8}{\sqrt{81 - 10 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$"] [:db/add "4a24f09e-263b-5efe-ac71-a976bc84e3aa" :question/worked-solution "First factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
\sqrt{81 - 10 x^{2}}=\sqrt{81(1-(\frac{10}{81})x^{2})}
$$

Use the linear substitution $u=\frac{\sqrt{10} x}{9}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{\sqrt{10}}{9},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\frac{9 \sqrt{10}}{10})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Change both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=- \frac{9 \sqrt{10}}{20}&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{\sqrt{10}}{9})(- \frac{9 \sqrt{10}}{20})=- \frac{1}{2} \\ x=\frac{9 \sqrt{5}}{10}&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{\sqrt{10}}{9})(\frac{9 \sqrt{5}}{10})=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Both transformed endpoints lie strictly between $-1$ and $1$, so the integrand is continuous throughout the interval.

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int_{- \frac{9 \sqrt{10}}{20}}^{\frac{9 \sqrt{5}}{10}} \frac{8}{\sqrt{81 - 10 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{8}{9}\int_{- \frac{9 \sqrt{10}}{20}}^{\frac{9 \sqrt{5}}{10}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(\frac{\sqrt{10} x}{9})^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{8}{9}(\frac{9 \sqrt{10}}{10})\int_{- \frac{1}{2}}^{\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{4 \sqrt{10}}{5}\int_{- \frac{1}{2}}^{\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{4 \sqrt{10}}{5}[\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}]_{- \frac{1}{2}}^{\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}} \\  &= \frac{4 \sqrt{10}}{5}(\operatorname{arcsin}(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})-\operatorname{arcsin}(- \frac{1}{2})) \\  &= \frac{4 \sqrt{10}}{5}((\frac{\pi}{4})-(- \frac{\pi}{6})) \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{10} \pi}{3}\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "4a24f09e-263b-5efe-ac71-a976bc84e3aa" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "4a24f09e-263b-5efe-ac71-a976bc84e3aa" :question/answer-fields Give an exact answer.

$$
\int_{\frac{8}{3}}^{\frac{8 \sqrt{3}}{3}} \frac{3}{3 x^{2} + 64}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$"] [:db/add "b7e7efd8-4daf-5a99-9901-08530da7dbd2" :question/worked-solution "First factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
3 x^{2} + 64=64(1+(\frac{3}{64})x^{2})
$$

Use the linear substitution $u=\frac{\sqrt{3} x}{8}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{8},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\frac{8 \sqrt{3}}{3})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Change both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\frac{8}{3}&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{8})(\frac{8}{3})=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3} \\ x=\frac{8 \sqrt{3}}{3}&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{8})(\frac{8 \sqrt{3}}{3})=1\end{aligned}
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int_{\frac{8}{3}}^{\frac{8 \sqrt{3}}{3}} \frac{3}{3 x^{2} + 64}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{3}{64}\int_{\frac{8}{3}}^{\frac{8 \sqrt{3}}{3}} \frac{1}{1+(\frac{\sqrt{3} x}{8})^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{3}{64}(\frac{8 \sqrt{3}}{3})\int_{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}}^{1} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{3}}{8}\int_{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}}^{1} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{3}}{8}[\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}]_{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}}^{1} \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{3}}{8}(\operatorname{arctan}(1)-\operatorname{arctan}(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3})) \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{3}}{8}((\frac{\pi}{4})-(\frac{\pi}{6})) \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{3} \pi}{96}\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "b7e7efd8-4daf-5a99-9901-08530da7dbd2" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "b7e7efd8-4daf-5a99-9901-08530da7dbd2" :question/answer-fields {{answer}}"] ["a2d73b9e-ded5-5263-8f8f-f603b91d7e83" :question/worked-solution "Use the linear substitution $u=5 x.$ Then

$$

$$

Change both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=0&\Longrightarrow u=(5)(0)=0 \\ x=\frac{1}{10}&\Longrightarrow u=(5)(\frac{1}{10})=\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Both transformed endpoints lie strictly between $-1$ and $1$, so the integrand is continuous throughout the interval.

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int_{0}^{\frac{1}{10}} \frac{4}{\sqrt{1 - 25 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 4\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{10}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(5 x)^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 4(\frac{1}{5})\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{4}{5}\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{4}{5}[\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}]_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}} \\  &= \frac{4}{5}(\operatorname{arcsin}(\frac{1}{2})-\operatorname{arcsin}(0)) \\  &= \frac{4}{5}((\frac{\pi}{6})-(0)) \\  &= \frac{2 \pi}{15}\end{aligned}
$$"] ["a2d73b9e-ded5-5263-8f8f-f603b91d7e83" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] ["a2d73b9e-ded5-5263-8f8f-f603b91d7e83" :question/answer-fields "aa4440e7-6f62-5402-bbe0-f2650309cdb7"] [17592186064220 :knowledge-point/questions "a2d73b9e-ded5-5263-8f8f-f603b91d7e83"] ["2a0125b7-63f0-5ffe-9867-939dcd35b2af" :answer/id #uuid "2a0125b7-63f0-5ffe-9867-939dcd35b2af"] ["2a0125b7-63f0-5ffe-9867-939dcd35b2af" :answer/type :answer.type/math] ["2a0125b7-63f0-5ffe-9867-939dcd35b2af" :answer/value "\frac{\pi}{4}"] ["e3ea9054-3361-5bd8-b506-dcb0dcac388a" :answer-field/id #uuid "e3ea9054-3361-5bd8-b506-dcb0dcac388a"] ["e3ea9054-3361-5bd8-b506-dcb0dcac388a" :answer-field/key "answer"] ["e3ea9054-3361-5bd8-b506-dcb0dcac388a" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/blank] ["e3ea9054-3361-5bd8-b506-dcb0dcac388a" :answer-field/choices "2a0125b7-63f0-5ffe-9867-939dcd35b2af"] ["e3ea9054-3361-5bd8-b506-dcb0dcac388a" :answer-field/correct "2a0125b7-63f0-5ffe-9867-939dcd35b2af"] ["a7b41060-9701-5ac8-9406-41c43c4a9895" :question/id #uuid "a7b41060-9701-5ac8-9406-41c43c4a9895"] ["a7b41060-9701-5ac8-9406-41c43c4a9895" :question/problem "Evaluate the integral. \int_{0}^{\frac{1}{16}} \frac{3}{\sqrt{1 - 64 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x

$$

Change both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=0&\Longrightarrow u=(8)(0)=0 \\ x=\frac{1}{16}&\Longrightarrow u=(8)(\frac{1}{16})=\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}

Both transformed endpoints lie strictly between $-1$ and $1$, so the integrand is continuous throughout the interval.

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int_{0}^{\frac{1}{16}} \frac{3}{\sqrt{1 - 64 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 3\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{16}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(8 x)^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 3(\frac{1}{8})\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{3}{8}\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{3}{8}[\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}]_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}} \\  &= \frac{3}{8}(\operatorname{arcsin}(\frac{1}{2})-\operatorname{arcsin}(0)) \\  &= \frac{3}{8}((\frac{\pi}{6})-(0)) \\  &= \frac{\pi}{16}\end{aligned}

Give an exact answer.

$$
\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{8}} \frac{9}{64 x^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$"] ["6871a209-fee3-5a51-a701-ff2bbca02c0a" :question/worked-solution "Use the linear substitution $u=8 x.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=8,\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\frac{1}{8})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Change both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=0&\Longrightarrow u=(8)(0)=0 \\ x=\frac{1}{8}&\Longrightarrow u=(8)(\frac{1}{8})=1\end{aligned}
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int_{0}^{\frac{1}{8}} \frac{9}{64 x^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 9\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{8}} \frac{1}{1+(8 x)^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 9(\frac{1}{8})\int_{0}^{1} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{9}{8}\int_{0}^{1} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{9}{8}[\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}]_{0}^{1} \\  &= \frac{9}{8}(\operatorname{arctan}(1)-\operatorname{arctan}(0)) \\  &= \frac{9}{8}((\frac{\pi}{4})-(0)) \\  &= \frac{9 \pi}{32}\end{aligned}
$$"] ["6871a209-fee3-5a51-a701-ff2bbca02c0a" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] ["6871a209-fee3-5a51-a701-ff2bbca02c0a" :question/answer-fields "234d093f-86d5-5259-9076-fc2ff176a74e"] \int_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}} \frac{8}{36 x^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}x

$$

$$

$$

Give an exact answer.

$$
\int_{0}^{3 \sqrt{2}} \frac{2}{x^{2} + 6}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$"] ["e251937d-16b7-5326-a140-cdc3ea29c25f" :question/worked-solution "First factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
x^{2} + 6=6(1+(\frac{1}{6})x^{2})
$$

Use the linear substitution $u=\frac{\sqrt{6} x}{6}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{\sqrt{6}}{6},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\sqrt{6})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Change both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=0&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{\sqrt{6}}{6})(0)=0 \\ x=3 \sqrt{2}&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{\sqrt{6}}{6})(3 \sqrt{2})=\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$

$$

{{answer}}"] ["21a4ebc8-c316-5cfd-93e4-ca1118604531" :question/worked-solution "First factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
x^{2} + 10=10(1+(\frac{1}{10})x^{2})
$$

Use the linear substitution $u=\frac{\sqrt{10} x}{10}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{\sqrt{10}}{10},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\sqrt{10})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Change both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=0&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{\sqrt{10}}{10})(0)=0 \\ x=\sqrt{10}&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{\sqrt{10}}{10})(\sqrt{10})=1\end{aligned}
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int_{0}^{\sqrt{10}} \frac{8}{x^{2} + 10}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{4}{5}\int_{0}^{\sqrt{10}} \frac{1}{1+(\frac{\sqrt{10} x}{10})^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{4}{5}(\sqrt{10})\int_{0}^{1} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{4 \sqrt{10}}{5}\int_{0}^{1} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{4 \sqrt{10}}{5}[\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}]_{0}^{1} \\  &= \frac{4 \sqrt{10}}{5}(\operatorname{arctan}(1)-\operatorname{arctan}(0)) \\  &= \frac{4 \sqrt{10}}{5}((\frac{\pi}{4})-(0)) \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{10} \pi}{5}\end{aligned}
$$"] ["21a4ebc8-c316-5cfd-93e4-ca1118604531" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] ["21a4ebc8-c316-5cfd-93e4-ca1118604531" :question/answer-fields "5a9796b7-f543-5dc8-b952-8b55e73eb6a2"] [17592186064220 :knowledge-point/questions "21a4ebc8-c316-5cfd-93e4-ca1118604531"] ["cf36209d-dd8d-57a1-a765-f750e1391b98" :answer/id #uuid "cf36209d-dd8d-57a1-a765-f750e1391b98"] ["cf36209d-dd8d-57a1-a765-f750e1391b98" :answer/type :answer.type/math] ["cf36209d-dd8d-57a1-a765-f750e1391b98" :answer/value "\pi"] ["b352b4d8-ef8e-542f-94af-6fac013fa473" :answer-field/id #uuid "b352b4d8-ef8e-542f-94af-6fac013fa473"] ["b352b4d8-ef8e-542f-94af-6fac013fa473" :answer-field/key "answer"] ["b352b4d8-ef8e-542f-94af-6fac013fa473" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/blank] ["b352b4d8-ef8e-542f-94af-6fac013fa473" :answer-field/choices "cf36209d-dd8d-57a1-a765-f750e1391b98"] ["b352b4d8-ef8e-542f-94af-6fac013fa473" :answer-field/correct "cf36209d-dd8d-57a1-a765-f750e1391b98"] ["561f8902-181d-50e5-8116-48d2cb1ddaae" :question/id #uuid "561f8902-181d-50e5-8116-48d2cb1ddaae"] ["561f8902-181d-50e5-8116-48d2cb1ddaae" :question/problem "Evaluate the integral. {{answer}}"] ["561f8902-181d-50e5-8116-48d2cb1ddaae" :question/worked-solution "First factor the constant in the denominator:

$$

$$

{{answer}}"] ["0372c2fd-66f2-541c-882f-7c71be7cc96e" :question/worked-solution "First factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
10 x^{2} + 9=9(1+(\frac{10}{9})x^{2})
$$

Use the linear substitution $u=\frac{\sqrt{10} x}{3}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{\sqrt{10}}{3},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\frac{3 \sqrt{10}}{10})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Change both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\frac{3 \sqrt{10}}{10}&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{\sqrt{10}}{3})(\frac{3 \sqrt{10}}{10})=1 \\ x=\frac{3 \sqrt{30}}{10}&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{\sqrt{10}}{3})(\frac{3 \sqrt{30}}{10})=\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int_{\frac{3 \sqrt{10}}{10}}^{\frac{3 \sqrt{30}}{10}} \frac{1}{10 x^{2} + 9}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{1}{9}\int_{\frac{3 \sqrt{10}}{10}}^{\frac{3 \sqrt{30}}{10}} \frac{1}{1+(\frac{\sqrt{10} x}{3})^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{1}{9}(\frac{3 \sqrt{10}}{10})\int_{1}^{\sqrt{3}} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{10}}{30}\int_{1}^{\sqrt{3}} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{10}}{30}[\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}]_{1}^{\sqrt{3}} \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{10}}{30}(\operatorname{arctan}(\sqrt{3})-\operatorname{arctan}(1)) \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{10}}{30}((\frac{\pi}{3})-(\frac{\pi}{4})) \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{10} \pi}{360}\end{aligned}
$$"] ["0372c2fd-66f2-541c-882f-7c71be7cc96e" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] ["0372c2fd-66f2-541c-882f-7c71be7cc96e" :question/answer-fields "b9486294-79c8-509d-84d4-b54229d994a1"] [17592186064220 :knowledge-point/questions "0372c2fd-66f2-541c-882f-7c71be7cc96e"] ["fdc0d3f5-a51b-5597-9b0f-2b50228b93a1" :answer/id #uuid "fdc0d3f5-a51b-5597-9b0f-2b50228b93a1"] ["fdc0d3f5-a51b-5597-9b0f-2b50228b93a1" :answer/type :answer.type/math] ["fdc0d3f5-a51b-5597-9b0f-2b50228b93a1" :answer/value "\frac{7 \sqrt{3} \pi}{54}"] ["d1b888f5-5707-53a5-b970-7313bcf41529" :answer-field/id #uuid "d1b888f5-5707-53a5-b970-7313bcf41529"] ["d1b888f5-5707-53a5-b970-7313bcf41529" :answer-field/key "answer"] ["d1b888f5-5707-53a5-b970-7313bcf41529" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/blank] ["d1b888f5-5707-53a5-b970-7313bcf41529" :answer-field/choices "fdc0d3f5-a51b-5597-9b0f-2b50228b93a1"] ["d1b888f5-5707-53a5-b970-7313bcf41529" :answer-field/correct "fdc0d3f5-a51b-5597-9b0f-2b50228b93a1"] ["5880c807-c10d-50e8-9d88-c434c7630fa9" :question/id #uuid "5880c807-c10d-50e8-9d88-c434c7630fa9"] ["5880c807-c10d-50e8-9d88-c434c7630fa9" :question/problem "Evaluate the integral. {{answer}}"] ["5880c807-c10d-50e8-9d88-c434c7630fa9" :question/worked-solution "First factor the constant in the denominator:

$$

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C.

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int_{- 3 \sqrt{3}}^{9} \frac{6}{3 x^{2} + 81}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{2}{27}\int_{- 3 \sqrt{3}}^{9} \frac{1}{1+(\frac{\sqrt{3} x}{9})^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{2}{27}(3 \sqrt{3})\int_{-1}^{\sqrt{3}} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{2 \sqrt{3}}{9}\int_{-1}^{\sqrt{3}} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{2 \sqrt{3}}{9}[\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}]_{-1}^{\sqrt{3}} \\  &= \frac{2 \sqrt{3}}{9}(\operatorname{arctan}(\sqrt{3})-\operatorname{arctan}(-1)) \\  &= \frac{2 \sqrt{3}}{9}((\frac{\pi}{3})-(- \frac{\pi}{4})) \\  &= \frac{7 \sqrt{3} \pi}{54}\end{aligned}

\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{8},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\frac{8 \sqrt{3}}{3})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Change both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\frac{8}{3}&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{8})(\frac{8}{3})=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3} \\ x=\frac{8 \sqrt{3}}{3}&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{8})(\frac{8 \sqrt{3}}{3})=1\end{aligned}
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int_{\frac{8}{3}}^{\frac{8 \sqrt{3}}{3}} \frac{3}{3 x^{2} + 64}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{3}{64}\int_{\frac{8}{3}}^{\frac{8 \sqrt{3}}{3}} \frac{1}{1+(\frac{\sqrt{3} x}{8})^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{3}{64}(\frac{8 \sqrt{3}}{3})\int_{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}}^{1} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{3}}{8}\int_{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}}^{1} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{3}}{8}[\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}]_{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}}^{1} \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{3}}{8}(\operatorname{arctan}(1)-\operatorname{arctan}(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3})) \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{3}}{8}((\frac{\pi}{4})-(\frac{\pi}{6})) \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{3} \pi}{96}\end{aligned}

"aa336cf9-b3b8-5d4a-a543-f9cee172da34" :question/math-academy-id "q-19394" :question/problem "Evaluate the integral $$
\displaystyle {\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{2}{\sqrt{2-{x}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x.
$$" :question/worked-solution "Let's rewrite our integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{2}{\sqrt{2-{x}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x & =2{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\cdot (1-{x}^{2}/2)}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{2}}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}/2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\sqrt{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(x/\sqrt{2})^{2}}}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

This integral resembles the basic integral for inverse sine,

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{u}^{2}}}\text{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(u)+C.
$$

The only difference is that instead of ${u}^{2}$ as the variable, we have ${\left(\frac{x}{\sqrt{2}}\right)}^{2}.$

So, let's substitute $u=\frac{x}{\sqrt{2}}.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\sqrt{2}\,\text{d}u.
$$

Before substituting, we use the table below to change the limits from $x$ to $u.$

| $x$ | $0$ | $1$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $0$ | $\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$ |

Using the above, we can now write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{2}{\sqrt{2-{x}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x & =\sqrt{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(x/\sqrt{2})^{2}}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\sqrt{2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{2}/2}\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{u}^{2}}}\cdot (\sqrt{2}\,\text{d}u) \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{2}/2}\frac{\text{d}u}{\sqrt{1-{u}^{2}}} \\  & =2\operatorname{arcsin}⁡u{|}_{0}^{\sqrt{2}/2} \\  & =2\operatorname{arcsin}⁡\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)-2\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(0) \\  & =2\cdot \frac{\pi }{4} \\  & =\frac{\pi }{2}\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186064545 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "3caebccd-a111-5c41-885b-601d0e3537ef" :answer/type {:db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "\frac{9}{2}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(14)" :db/id 17592186285359} {:answer/id #uuid "5c49b8ca-6a4c-5d5b-bee0-678ddd9d003c" :answer/type {:db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "\frac{9}{4}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(7)" :db/id 17592186285633} {:answer/id #uuid "77e0a940-8e6f-54a7-9506-301d4949f5ee" :answer/type {:db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "\frac{9}{2}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(7)" :db/id 17592186285904} {:answer/id #uuid "c96c9e76-bbaf-5ac6-a64e-a08681842df9" :answer/type {:db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "\frac{9}{4}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(14)" :db/id 17592186286625} {:answer/id #uuid "eda35d92-71e9-5870-9644-e45103f5e6c2" :answer/type {:db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "9\operatorname{arctan}⁡(14)" :db/id 17592186286967}] :answer-field/correct {:answer/id #uuid "c96c9e76-bbaf-5ac6-a64e-a08681842df9" :answer/type {:db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "\frac{9}{4}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(14)" :db/id 17592186286625} :answer-field/id #uuid "23ae6c57-6433-571b-8f19-8245bed72d97" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/ident :answer-field.type/radio} :db/id 17592186287223}] :question/difficulty {:db/ident :question.difficulty/moderate} :question/id #uuid "4167c2cd-a204-5a1b-9ee4-1fca54336ae6" :question/math-academy-id "q-19397" :question/problem "Evaluate the integral $$
\displaystyle {\int }_{0}^{7}\frac{9}{2+8{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x.
$$" :question/worked-solution "Note that we can rewrite this integral as

$$
{\int }_{0}^{7}\frac{9}{2+8{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{9}{2}{\int }_{0}^{7}\frac{1}{1+4{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x.
$$

This integral resembles the basic integral for inverse tangent,

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+{u}^{2}}\text{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}⁡u+C.
$$

The only difference is that instead of ${u}^{2}$ as the variable, we have $4{x}^{2}=(2x)^{2}.$

So, let's substitute $u=2x.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{2}\text{d}u.
$$

Before substituting, we use the table below to change the limits from $x$ to $u.$

| $x$ | $0$ | $7$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $0$ | $14$ |

Using the above, we can now write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

\displaystyle {\int }_{-0.25}^{0.25}\frac{3}{\sqrt{3-12{x}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x.
$$" :question/worked-solution "Let's rewrite our integral as follows:

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{6}} \frac{7}{\sqrt{1 - 9 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Use the linear substitution $u=3 x.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=3,\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\frac{1}{3})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Change both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=0&\Longrightarrow u=(3)(0)=0 \\ x=\frac{1}{6}&\Longrightarrow u=(3)(\frac{1}{6})=\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Both transformed endpoints lie strictly between $-1$ and $1$, so the integrand is continuous throughout the interval.

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int_{0}^{\frac{1}{6}} \frac{7}{\sqrt{1 - 9 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 7\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{6}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(3 x)^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 7(\frac{1}{3})\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{7}{3}\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{7}{3}[\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}]_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}} \\  &= \frac{7}{3}(\operatorname{arcsin}(\frac{1}{2})-\operatorname{arcsin}(0)) \\  &= \frac{7}{3}((\frac{\pi}{6})-(0)) \\  &= \frac{7 \pi}{18}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{6}} \frac{8}{36 x^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Use the linear substitution $u=6 x.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=6,\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\frac{1}{6})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Change both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=0&\Longrightarrow u=(6)(0)=0 \\ x=\frac{1}{6}&\Longrightarrow u=(6)(\frac{1}{6})=1\end{aligned}
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int_{0}^{\frac{1}{6}} \frac{8}{36 x^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 8\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{6}} \frac{1}{1+(6 x)^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 8(\frac{1}{6})\int_{0}^{1} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{4}{3}\int_{0}^{1} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{4}{3}[\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}]_{0}^{1} \\  &= \frac{4}{3}(\operatorname{arctan}(1)-\operatorname{arctan}(0)) \\  &= \frac{4}{3}((\frac{\pi}{4})-(0)) \\  &= \frac{\pi}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int_{0}^{\sqrt{5}} \frac{4}{\sqrt{10 - x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

{{answer}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
First factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
\sqrt{10 - x^{2}}=\sqrt{10(1-(\frac{1}{10})x^{2})}
$$

Use the linear substitution $u=\frac{\sqrt{10} x}{10}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{\sqrt{10}}{10},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\sqrt{10})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Change both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=0&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{\sqrt{10}}{10})(0)=0 \\ x=\sqrt{5}&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{\sqrt{10}}{10})(\sqrt{5})=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Both transformed endpoints lie strictly between $-1$ and $1$, so the integrand is continuous throughout the interval.

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int_{0}^{\sqrt{5}} \frac{4}{\sqrt{10 - x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{2 \sqrt{10}}{5}\int_{0}^{\sqrt{5}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(\frac{\sqrt{10} x}{10})^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{2 \sqrt{10}}{5}(\sqrt{10})\int_{0}^{\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= 4\int_{0}^{\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= 4[\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}]_{0}^{\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}} \\  &= 4(\operatorname{arcsin}(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})-\operatorname{arcsin}(0)) \\  &= 4((\frac{\pi}{4})-(0)) \\  &= \pi\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int_{0}^{\frac{8 \sqrt{3}}{3}} \frac{6}{x^{2} + 64}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

{{answer}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
First factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
x^{2} + 64=64(1+(\frac{1}{64})x^{2})
$$

Use the linear substitution $u=\frac{x}{8}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{1}{8},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(8)\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Change both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=0&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{1}{8})(0)=0 \\ x=\frac{8 \sqrt{3}}{3}&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{1}{8})(\frac{8 \sqrt{3}}{3})=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int_{0}^{\frac{8 \sqrt{3}}{3}} \frac{6}{x^{2} + 64}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{3}{32}\int_{0}^{\frac{8 \sqrt{3}}{3}} \frac{1}{1+(\frac{x}{8})^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{3}{32}(8)\int_{0}^{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{3}{4}\int_{0}^{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{3}{4}[\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}]_{0}^{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}} \\  &= \frac{3}{4}(\operatorname{arctan}(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3})-\operatorname{arctan}(0)) \\  &= \frac{3}{4}((\frac{\pi}{6})-(0)) \\  &= \frac{\pi}{8}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int_{- \frac{7}{2}}^{\frac{7}{2}} \frac{6}{\sqrt{49 - x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

{{answer}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
First factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
\sqrt{49 - x^{2}}=\sqrt{49(1-(\frac{1}{49})x^{2})}
$$

Use the linear substitution $u=\frac{x}{7}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{1}{7},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(7)\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Change both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=- \frac{7}{2}&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{1}{7})(- \frac{7}{2})=- \frac{1}{2} \\ x=\frac{7}{2}&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{1}{7})(\frac{7}{2})=\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Both transformed endpoints lie strictly between $-1$ and $1$, so the integrand is continuous throughout the interval.

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int_{- \frac{7}{2}}^{\frac{7}{2}} \frac{6}{\sqrt{49 - x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{6}{7}\int_{- \frac{7}{2}}^{\frac{7}{2}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(\frac{x}{7})^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{6}{7}(7)\int_{- \frac{1}{2}}^{\frac{1}{2}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= 6\int_{- \frac{1}{2}}^{\frac{1}{2}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= 6[\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}]_{- \frac{1}{2}}^{\frac{1}{2}} \\  &= 6(\operatorname{arcsin}(\frac{1}{2})-\operatorname{arcsin}(- \frac{1}{2})) \\  &= 6((\frac{\pi}{6})-(- \frac{\pi}{6})) \\  &= 2 \pi\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{\sqrt{7}}{5},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\frac{5 \sqrt{7}}{7})\,\mathrm{d}u.

$$

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C.

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int_{\frac{5 \sqrt{21}}{21}}^{\frac{5 \sqrt{7}}{7}} \frac{9}{7 x^{2} + 25}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{9}{25}\int_{\frac{5 \sqrt{21}}{21}}^{\frac{5 \sqrt{7}}{7}} \frac{1}{1+(\frac{\sqrt{7} x}{5})^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{9}{25}(\frac{5 \sqrt{7}}{7})\int_{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}}^{1} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{9 \sqrt{7}}{35}\int_{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}}^{1} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{9 \sqrt{7}}{35}[\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}]_{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}}^{1} \\  &= \frac{9 \sqrt{7}}{35}(\operatorname{arctan}(1)-\operatorname{arctan}(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3})) \\  &= \frac{9 \sqrt{7}}{35}((\frac{\pi}{4})-(\frac{\pi}{6})) \\  &= \frac{3 \sqrt{7} \pi}{140}\end{aligned}

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int_{- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{3}}^{\frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}} \frac{2}{6 x^{2} + 4}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
6 x^{2} + 4=4(1+(\frac{3}{2})x^{2})
$$

Use the linear substitution $u=\frac{\sqrt{6} x}{2}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{\sqrt{6}}{2},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\frac{\sqrt{6}}{3})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Change both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{3}&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{\sqrt{6}}{2})(- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{3})=- \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3} \\ x=\frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{\sqrt{6}}{2})(\frac{\sqrt{6}}{3})=1\end{aligned}
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int_{- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{3}}^{\frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}} \frac{2}{6 x^{2} + 4}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{1}{2}\int_{- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{3}}^{\frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}} \frac{1}{1+(\frac{\sqrt{6} x}{2})^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{1}{2}(\frac{\sqrt{6}}{3})\int_{- \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}}^{1} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{6}}{6}\int_{- \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}}^{1} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{6}}{6}[\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}]_{- \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}}^{1} \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{6}}{6}(\operatorname{arctan}(1)-\operatorname{arctan}(- \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3})) \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{6}}{6}((\frac{\pi}{4})-(- \frac{\pi}{6})) \\  &= \frac{5 \sqrt{6} \pi}{72}\end{aligned}

\begin{aligned}& \int_{- 3 \sqrt{3}}^{9} \frac{6}{3 x^{2} + 81}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{2}{27}\int_{- 3 \sqrt{3}}^{9} \frac{1}{1+(\frac{\sqrt{3} x}{9})^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{2}{27}(3 \sqrt{3})\int_{-1}^{\sqrt{3}} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{2 \sqrt{3}}{9}\int_{-1}^{\sqrt{3}} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{2 \sqrt{3}}{9}[\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}]_{-1}^{\sqrt{3}} \\  &= \frac{2 \sqrt{3}}{9}(\operatorname{arctan}(\sqrt{3})-\operatorname{arctan}(-1)) \\  &= \frac{2 \sqrt{3}}{9}((\frac{\pi}{3})-(- \frac{\pi}{4})) \\  &= \frac{7 \sqrt{3} \pi}{54}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int_{\frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}}^{\frac{2 \sqrt{3}}{3}} \frac{2}{\sqrt{16 - 6 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

{{answer}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
First factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
\sqrt{16 - 6 x^{2}}=\sqrt{16(1-(\frac{3}{8})x^{2})}
$$

Use the linear substitution $u=\frac{\sqrt{6} x}{4}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{\sqrt{6}}{4},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\frac{2 \sqrt{6}}{3})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Change both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{\sqrt{6}}{4})(\frac{\sqrt{6}}{3})=\frac{1}{2} \\ x=\frac{2 \sqrt{3}}{3}&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{\sqrt{6}}{4})(\frac{2 \sqrt{3}}{3})=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Both transformed endpoints lie strictly between $-1$ and $1$, so the integrand is continuous throughout the interval.

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int_{\frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}}^{\frac{2 \sqrt{3}}{3}} \frac{2}{\sqrt{16 - 6 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{1}{2}\int_{\frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}}^{\frac{2 \sqrt{3}}{3}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(\frac{\sqrt{6} x}{4})^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{1}{2}(\frac{2 \sqrt{6}}{3})\int_{\frac{1}{2}}^{\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}\int_{\frac{1}{2}}^{\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}[\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}]_{\frac{1}{2}}^{\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}} \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}(\operatorname{arcsin}(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})-\operatorname{arcsin}(\frac{1}{2})) \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}((\frac{\pi}{4})-(\frac{\pi}{6})) \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{6} \pi}{36}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
3 x^{2} + 64=64(1+(\frac{3}{64})x^{2})
$$

Use the linear substitution $u=\frac{\sqrt{3} x}{8}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{8},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\frac{8 \sqrt{3}}{3})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Change both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\frac{8}{3}&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{8})(\frac{8}{3})=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3} \\ x=\frac{8 \sqrt{3}}{3}&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{8})(\frac{8 \sqrt{3}}{3})=1\end{aligned}
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int_{\frac{8}{3}}^{\frac{8 \sqrt{3}}{3}} \frac{3}{3 x^{2} + 64}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{3}{64}\int_{\frac{8}{3}}^{\frac{8 \sqrt{3}}{3}} \frac{1}{1+(\frac{\sqrt{3} x}{8})^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{3}{64}(\frac{8 \sqrt{3}}{3})\int_{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}}^{1} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{3}}{8}\int_{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}}^{1} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{3}}{8}[\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}]_{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}}^{1} \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{3}}{8}(\operatorname{arctan}(1)-\operatorname{arctan}(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3})) \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{3}}{8}((\frac{\pi}{4})-(\frac{\pi}{6})) \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{3} \pi}{96}\end{aligned}
$$
